★ Boom candidates (small caps first)

What is this?

These are stocks that could benefit if the related story happens. Confirmed means the price has already made the scan's qualifying move; waiting means it has not. Open a row for the plain-language reason, current price, stop, risk and catalyst.

17 confirmed · 2 waiting · 2 large caps · 49 watchlist

Row: rank · ✓ confirmed / … waiting · ticker + name · Nd = days in a row Confirmed · upside estimate; second line: market cap · risk to stop · catalyst date · latest price (USD · CAD) · LF = low float

Stops are locked where first shown; a red badge means price closed below it.

Each pick keeps the stop it had the first time it appeared (🔒 date). It is never lowered after a drop. If a daily close is at or below it, the row gets a red “Stop hit” badge that stays; the pick stays visible but has no upside/risk ratio.

ⓘ How this works

Stocks with the biggest upside if a narrative from your posts plays out. "Since the call" = first close after the post to the latest close. Research only, not advice; the stop is where the story looks wrong, not a trade instruction. Tap a row to open the full card.

How ranked (small caps first, Oct 2): 1) filters: late calls (20%+ run in the prior month), price broken since the call, or under $2M/day traded go to the watchlist. 2) confirmation: Confirmed once the price moves with the story after the call (a day up 5%+ on 1.5× average volume, or a close above its 20-day high). 3) Confirmed names are ranked by upside ÷ risk × size weight (under $2B ×2.0, $2-10B ×1.4, $10-200B ×0.85); mega caps over $200B move to the Large caps strip at the bottom. Upside estimate = half the way back to the 52-week high + half the analyst mean target (capped +50%; ignored if stale or under $1B with < 4 analysts); risk = distance to a story-wrong stop (the tighter of 1% below the pre-call low and 2× the 14-day ATR). Waiting names: combined score × the same size weight. Low-float names are flagged. Backtest (top 5 per week, 1-month excess vs S&P, pop/bust ±20%): small-cap version -1.8% avg, 44% hit, pop 7%, bust 10% (n=269); previous combined -0.3% avg, 48% hit, pop 9%, bust 8% (n=341) (difference -3.7 to +0.8 pts, mostly from moving mega caps out). Confirmation does fix small caps: confirmed small caps -0.2% avg, 44% hit, pop 15%, bust 16% (n=80) vs all small-cap calls -5.0% avg, 34% hit, pop 11%, bust 28% (n=271). Earlier ranks (v4 / upside / echo / old) are on each card and in api/candidates.json.

Glossary
Confirmed
The price made the scan's qualifying move after the call.
Days on list
How many days in a row it has stayed Confirmed (from daily published snapshots).
Waiting
The idea is still being watched; that qualifying move has not happened.
Stop
A story-wrong level where the idea would look invalid; it is not an instruction to sell.
Risk %
How far the latest price is above that stop.
Upside est.
A rough room-to-run estimate using the 52-week high and analyst data where allowed.
Up/risk ratio
Estimated upside divided by risk to the stop; higher is better for this ranking.
Short % of float
The share of tradable shares sold short, which can add fuel but also signals skepticism.
Days to cover
Approximate trading days for short sellers to buy back their shares.
Low float
Few tradable shares, so the price can swing sharply both ways.
Source grade A–D
A quick read of evidence quality and independence; it only nudges the rank.
Copycats / echo
Later posts repeating an earlier idea; many repeats are not many independent discoveries.
Vs S&P
The stock return minus the S&P 500 return over the same period.

4 · Sources / accounts

What is this?

These are the accounts and posts behind the ideas. Independent accounts count more than repeated copycat posts; the price record shows what happened after each call.

ⓘ How this works

Post dates are decoded from the X post IDs (ET). tentative = handle-to-event match not confirmed. Records only count confirmed matches and only the source's own picks (not my DRAFT additions), using the source's direction; the scoreboard will need ~20 resolved calls per source before a hit rate means much.

Intraday reactions (for algos)

What is this?

This checks how a stock traded in the first minutes and hours after a post named it. Compare the move with SPY over the same window; small samples and missing bars make this a rough read, not a trading signal.

ⓘ How this works

How each ticker traded right after the post that named it, vs SPY over the same minutes. Base = open of the first bar after the post (next open if posted outside the session). +1d = through the next session's close; "close" = same session's close. Bars from Yahoo (unofficial): 1-minute for posts under ~30 days old, 5-minute under ~60 days, hourly older. Hit = beat SPY (assumes the mention was bullish). 2040 of 2179 post-ticker pairs have bars (1m: 237, 5m: 333, 60m: 1470, none: 139). Blank = no data, nothing filled in. Small samples: early reads only.

History · what was ranked where

What is this?
Tap a day to see how the Picks list was ranked that evening (the last refresh of the day). Each row shows the price that day and the latest price, so you can see how each pick did since. new = entered the top 10 that day. A grey tag means it has since dropped out of the top 10 (its rank now, or watch / big cap). The ranking rules changed on the evening of Oct 2: the chip “Oct 2 · old” is the last list under the old rules (how strong the story and its source looked); later days rank by upside ÷ risk after the price confirms, small caps first. Research only, not advice.
